sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and options
sections.what: Explains that the tool prints a copy of the token variables for standalone HTML, with three options: full output, minimal output, and wrapping in a style tag.
sections.why: Likely reason: standalone files cannot read the project's CSS, so the values must be copied into them.
sections.watch_out: The output is a snapshot, so the script must be run again after the token file changes.

sections.name: findProjectRoot
sections.title: Finding the project's token file
sections.what: Searches upward from the current folder for the assets folder containing the token CSS file. It stops the script with an error if it cannot find one.
sections.why: Lets the tool run from any folder inside the project.
sections.watch_out: The search stops only when it reaches the Unix root, so on systems with other root names it may never stop.

sections.name: MINIMAL_TOKENS
sections.title: Prefixes for the minimal set
sections.what: Lists the name fragments of the variables most used in slides and infographics, such as spacing, font size, shadows, and main colors.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps standalone files small by copying only what they usually need.
sections.watch_out: Matching checks whether a name contains the fragment, so a renamed variable can drop out without any error.

sections.name: extractTokens
sections.title: Pulling out the variables
sections.what: Finds the root block in the CSS, collects its variable lines, keeps only the minimal set when asked, removes duplicates, and returns a single root block. It returns nothing if no root block exists.
sections.why: Produces the copied values that the output is built from.
sections.watch_out: Pattern matching can miss variables that are split across lines or written in a different layout.

summary: Copies the design token variables from the token CSS file and prints them so they can be pasted into a standalone HTML file.
purpose: Lets standalone HTML files such as infographics and slides use the same design values as the project, without linking to the project files.
why: Likely reason: a standalone file cannot read the project's CSS, so the values are copied in.
how: The script searches upward from the current folder for the token CSS file, stopping with an error if none is found. It reads the root block, optionally keeps only the commonly used variables, removes duplicates, and prints the result with an optional style tag wrapper.
inputs: The assets/design-tokens.css file in the project, found by searching upward, and the minimal and style options.
outputs: A text block printed to the terminal. It writes no files.
risks: The output is a copy, so later changes to the token file are not reflected until the script is run again. Matching by text may miss variables written in unusual layouts.
debug: If the script reports that the token file was not found, run it from inside the project. If variables are missing from the minimal output, check the list of prefixes. If a variable is missing entirely, check the token file for it.
